_about: Contextual mind-meld questions for the CCR Suggested-merges worklist. The 🧠 Mind-meld panel (unified_courses.js) matches each group's computed features against `trigger` and surfaces matching questions; Sam answers by voice/text and the note lands in Supabase merge_doctrine_notes tagged with the question id. Answers are distilled into kb/merge_doctrine.md at checkpoints. Triggers: level_ladder, skill_strands, credit_noncredit_mix, units_spread, same_college, cross_discipline, generic_title, honors_variant, esl_language, activity_ladder, big_group, always.

questions.question: This looks like a level ladder. Package into Beginning/Intermediate/Advanced, or keep the rungs? What signal are you using — degree-applicability, credit status, whether a credential could map to a single rung?
These differentiate skill strands (reading/writing/grammar/conversation…). Do strands fold into the level band, or is any strand its own credit target?

Credit and noncredit versions are both in play here. Separate targets forever, or should the noncredit twin fold under the credit target with a note? What would the credit recommendation actually award?
Unit loads differ across these members. At what spread would you stop merging — and does it matter whether the curriculum is externally standardized (BAR/POST/NCCER)?
All members are from one college. Is there any same-college case you'd merge outright (catalog editions, renumberings), or is this always variants to package or keep?
This group spans disciplines. Same course tagged inconsistently, or a homonym? If you merge it, which discipline should the survivor carry, and why?
Generic-title family (special topics / work experience / independent study). Umbrella-mint one per discipline, leave standalone, or exclude from the CPL-facing tier entirely?
An Honors (or Lab/Refresher/Instructor) variant sits next to its base. For CPL purposes does the variant fold under the base course, or stay its own target?
Activity family (sport/dance/music ensemble). One CCR row per activity regardless of level/gender/season, or finer? What would a credential ever map to here?
If this mints a package, how should it be named — clean band ("Beginning ESL") or explicit fold ("ESL — Beginning (Levels 1–2)")?
What went through your mind deciding this one? Anything the doctrine doesn't capture yet — say it here.
